issues.reason: Right that "record" is none of the named collective verbs, but the stated test is "each member acts separately" versus "the group as one unit", and "her logs record that P" is an aggregate fact about the corpus - the per-member rule would assert that EVERY individual log records P, content the text does not state, which the no-over-assertion rule bars outright.

gaps_confirmed: Factivity default for a clausal-complement verb on neither stated list ("record" is on neither the non-factive believe/think/say list nor the factive know/realize/regret list), so nothing decides whether P is also asserted at top level.
new_gaps: The distributive-vs-collective test is unsettled for an aggregate INFORMATIONAL predicate over a plural set of artifacts (logs/records/tables "record / show / list / state" P): the named collective verbs are all reciprocal (gather, meet, assemble, collide), so a corpus-level predicate falls between the two branches.

A sealed proposition carries no truth value of its own, so a kind-level relational generic sealed under Theme silently loses the (STV 0.9 0.9) its own doctrine mandates - the seal grammar has no slot for P's strength/confidence.
notes: The multi-word Name with no invented kind atom, the possessed-plural group witness with Possession, Experiencer on the seal-bearing holder, the sky_cat genus projecting out of the seal (explicitly licensed), and (Hunt sky_cat insect) as P's bare-kind relational form all follow the instruction set.
